status_values.Yes: Built in and documented by the vendor (feature page, help center, release notes or app store listing).
status_values.Partial: Exists but limited, e.g. only some service lines, only via workaround, or missing a key part of the definition. Explain in notes.
status_values.Add-on: Available only as a paid add-on module, higher tier, or through a named third-party integration. Name it in notes.
status_values.No: Vendor documentation or credible reviews show it is not offered.
status_values.Unknown: Could not confirm either way from public sources. Use this rather than guessing.

features.definition: Leads tracked through stages from first contact to signed customer.
Source recorded per lead; reports on close rate or revenue by source or campaign.
Build and send quotes, ideally with tiered (good, better, best) options.
Customer signs the service agreement electronically inside the product.
Mobile tool for field sales reps: territory maps, knock tracking, sign-up at the door.
Commission rules for reps or technicians, including holds or chargebacks on early cancellation.
Email or SMS sequences for quote follow-up, upsells, renewals or win-backs.
Cancellation reason codes, save attempts, retention tracking.
One billing account with many service locations (landlord, property manager, chain).
Click to call, call tracking, call recording or caller ID pop of the customer record.
Apartment and condo buildings served unit by unit, with unit access notes, per-unit history and resident contacts for notices.
Measure square footage, perimeter or lot size from aerial or satellite imagery to price or diagram a property without a site visit.
Leads from marketplaces such as Google Local Services, Angi or Thumbtack flow straight into the pipeline with their source.
Agreements with flexible cadence (monthly, every other month, quarterly, custom) that generate visits.
Fixed number of service rounds inside a date window, such as a mosquito and tick season.

features.feature: Price book with tiers and add-ons
features.definition: Prices by property size or tier, plus add-on items, maintained centrally.
Apply yearly price increases across many agreements at once.
Term length, auto-renewal, early cancellation fees tracked per agreement.
Termite or other warranties with yearly renewal billing and reminders.
Free return visits logged against the agreement, with their cost captured.
Visits created automatically from agreements into due windows.
Drag and drop scheduling board with a map view.
Automatic sequencing or assignment of stops to minimize drive time.
Scheduler considers technician skills, certifications or licenses when assigning work.
Customers can book or reschedule appointments themselves online.
Live technician or vehicle location for dispatchers.
Move many appointments at once, e.g. for weather.
Several technicians on one visit, each with a role such as lead, applicator, supervisor or helper, recorded on the visit.
Visits promised in a time window such as morning or afternoon, honored by dispatch and shown to the customer.
Suggests nearby customers or due visits to fill open slots or cancellations on a technician's day.
iOS and Android technician app.
Technicians can complete work without a connection and sync later.

features.feature: Product usage capture at the visit
features.definition: Technician records products, amounts and areas treated on the visit.
Capture photos, notes and a customer signature on the job.
Scan device or station barcodes in the field.
Collect card, check or cash payments from the app.
Clock in and out, track hours for payroll.
Technician sees and updates the stock on their vehicle.
Tenant-built forms and checklists (inspections, WDI, prep checklists) filled in the field and attached to the visit or customer.

features.feature: Languages other than English in the technician app
features.definition: The technician app can run in Spanish or another language besides English.
Application records meeting state requirements, generated from visit data.

features.feature: Product catalog with EPA numbers, labels and SDS
features.definition: Master list of products with EPA registration numbers, label and safety data sheet documents.
Technician license and certification numbers, categories and expiry alerts.
Reports or exports formatted for state pesticide regulators or inspections.
Pre- or post-application notices to customers or residents sent automatically.
Limits on who may apply restricted-use products, or RUP-specific record fields.
Stock by warehouse or branch, purchasing, transfers, usage deduction.

Each state's rules applied in the workflow: required record fields, customer and resident notice timing, notification registries, posting signs and seasonal blackouts, maintained per state. Yes needs rules for several states applied automatically; a few state report formats alone is Partial.
Weather, wind speed and direction, or temperature captured with the application, entered or pulled automatically.

features.feature: Mix and dilution calculator with label rate checks
features.definition: Calculates mixes and dilutions and warns when amounts or rates fall outside the product label.
Continuing-education or recertification credits tracked per applicator against renewal requirements.

features.feature: Device and station inventory per site
features.definition: Bait stations, traps and insect light traps tracked per site, usually with barcodes.
Floor plan or site map showing device locations, maintained in the product.
Per-device activity history and trend reports over time.
Audit-ready documentation for AIB, SQF, BRC or similar food safety audits.
Commercial customers access service reports, maps, labels and SDS online.
Customer pest sighting logs and recommendations tracked to closure.
PO numbers, net terms and consolidated invoices across sites.
Connected traps or sensors report rodent or insect activity into the device history without a site visit.
Termite graphs or diagrams, bait station monitoring, wood-destroying insect inspection reports.
Multi-visit trapping, exclusion and repair jobs with materials.
Multi-visit treatments with customer prep checklists.
Seasonal mosquito and tick programs.
Integration with a manufacturer termite bait program, such as Sentricon with Corteva reporting.
Card and ACH processing built in.
Saved payment methods charged automatically.
Per visit, flat monthly and annual prepay billing for the same service.
Tax rates by service address, with taxability set per service type.
Dunning reminders, payment retries, late fees, service holds for past-due accounts.
Account statements combining many invoices or agreements.
Automatic proration or balance due when an agreement is cancelled.
Saved cards are refreshed automatically when the issuer replaces them, so autopay keeps working.
Customers can finance larger jobs or pay over time through a built-in or partner lender.
Card surcharges or convenience fees, customer tips, or deposits collected on estimates.
Full double-entry accounting inside the product (not just an export).
Sync to QuickBooks Online or Desktop.
Sage, Xero, NetSuite or similar.
Prepayments held as deferred revenue and recognized as visits are performed.
Labor and material cost per job, with margin.
Payroll export or integration, including production-based technician pay.
Customers pay, see history and request service online.
Automatic appointment reminders and technician en route notices.
Office staff can text back and forth with customers.
Automated requests for online reviews after service.
Service report sent to the customer after the visit, listing products applied.
Letters, notices or invoices printed and mailed from the product, directly or through a mail service.
Satisfaction or NPS surveys after service, or a referral program that tracks and rewards referrals.
Revenue, AR aging, production and similar reports.
Retention or cancellation rates by route, technician, service or period.
Revenue or stops per technician, time on site, re-service rates.
User-built reports, dashboards or BI export.
Several branches or locations with separate settings and reporting.
Configurable roles controlling what each user can see and do.
Public or partner API, webhooks, or Zapier.
Vendor imports data from a previous system.
Any AI assistant, AI call answering, AI summaries, predictions or similar.
Hosted website, embeddable booking or lead forms.

features.feature: Marketing tools (direct mail, call tracking, SEO)
features.definition: Built-in marketing services beyond email and SMS campaigns.
Internal tasks and follow-ups for office staff, or a shared inbox that keeps customer messages on one timeline.
Users can see who changed what on a customer, agreement, visit or record, and when.

scope: Pest control only. Lawn care, tree and shrub care, and other trades are out of scope; products that serve them are compared on their pest features only.
